technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Framework's plugin mechanism for processor modules, allowing configuration via minimal class specification and module option commands.
Upgrade to Reactor 2.0 RC1, managing API breaking changes through compatibility layer or direct code migration.
Port existing Spring XD aggregation counter specs to Redis, leveraging Spring Data Redis for field-value counter operations.
Isolate Hadoop tests by creating a separate Maven/Gradle project to avoid dependency pollution in Eclipse and other IDEs.
Set up acceptance test infrastructure for XD on YARN using EC2, including provisioning scripts and CI integration.
Implement RxJava processor module following similar plugin design as Reactor, exposing RxJava APIs for data computations.
Expose HTTP source message size limit as a configurable property in servers.yml, using Spring Boot's @ConfigurationProperties.
All development will target Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0.
assumptions: Developer has existing knowledge of Spring XD codebase and its build system (Maven/Gradle).
The Reactor 2.0 RC1 release is stable enough for production upgrade and all API changes are documented.
Redis instance is available for development and testing; no additional infrastructure setup time beyond estimates.
Hadoop tests isolation does not require changes to the main source code, only test movement and build refinements.
AC2 acceptance test scripts can be reused from existing patterns; minor customization needed.
All user stories are independent and can be developed sequentially without blocking dependencies.
Documentation updates follow existing style and are considered part of the story effort.
No additional code reviews or management overhead beyond the developer’s own work.
